welcome:
Welcome to the DNS / curl / dig CLI Playground.
Type commands to explore a simulated network debugging environment.
Type 'help' for available commands, 'scenario' for guided labs.

steps.instruction: Users report they cannot reach api.example.com. Start by querying the A record.
The ANSWER section is empty — NXDOMAIN. Check if the authoritative nameservers know about it.
Let's query a public resolver directly to rule out local DNS cache issues.
Still failing. Trace the full resolution path to find where it breaks.
The trace shows the .com TLD delegates to ns1.example.com, but that nameserver isn't responding. Verify with nslookup.
Connection timed out to ns1.example.com. Check if that nameserver is reachable on port 53.
Port 53 is unreachable — the nameserver is down. Check the SOA record via the backup nameserver to confirm zone config.
ns2 responds! The zone exists but ns1 is down. Verify the domain resolves via ns2.
The monitoring dashboard shows 502 errors on https://api.example.com/health. Start with a verbose curl to see what's happening.
The response shows 502 Bad Gateway from the load balancer. Check if DNS is resolving correctly.
DNS resolves to 93.184.216.34. Check if the backend port is open.
Port 443 is open. Let's inspect the TLS certificate to rule out cert issues.
Certificate is valid. Let's check response timing to see where the delay is.
Connection is fast but time_starttransfer is 30s — the backend is timing out. Try hitting the backend directly bypassing the load balancer.
Direct backend also times out. The application itself is unhealthy. Check the other backend node.
Second backend responds with 200! The issue is isolated to 10.0.1.42. Confirm with a simple connectivity test.

commands.help:
Available commands:
  dig [domain]                   — Query DNS records (A, MX, NS, SOA, PTR, ANY)
  dig @[server] [domain]         — Query specific nameserver
  dig +short / +trace            — Short output / trace resolution path
  dig -x [IP]                    — Reverse DNS lookup (PTR)
  nslookup [domain]              — Simple DNS lookup
  curl [url]                     — Transfer data from URL
  curl -v / -I / -X / -d / -H   — Verbose / headers-only / method / data / header
  host [domain]                  — Simple DNS lookup
  whois [domain]                 — Domain registration info
  ping [host]                    — ICMP connectivity test
  traceroute [host]              — Trace packet route
  nc -zv [host] [port]           — Test TCP port connectivity
  openssl s_client               — TLS/SSL connection test

  scenario                       — Start a guided lab
  clear                          — Clear the terminal
  help                           — Show this help
